# Robotics Tracker

> This site tracks US and Chinese robotics. On the measures tracked here, the US leads on AI and capital and China on installations and the supply chain; whether either lead matters more is an open question. The site tracks what can be measured, shows its sources, and labels its own judgment calls.

Short form: **Where AI meets the physical world.**

A curated, continuously updated tracker of US and Chinese robotics and the US
policy that shapes it. **Every record carries at least one cited source URL, and
primary sources are preferred — but not every citation is primary.** Policy
records generally cite the Federal Register or the bill itself; company funding
and valuation figures often cite the outlet that reported them (TechCrunch,
Bloomberg, Reuters) because no primary filing exists. Follow the record's own
`sources[]` and judge the citation you actually get. Maintained by one curator,
not an institution; the whole dataset and site source are public.

Site: https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/
Source: https://github.com/pranava0x0/roboticsleadership

## How to read this site

The pages render their data client-side with JavaScript. If you do not execute
JS, **read the JSON files below instead** — they are the same data the pages
draw from, and they are the canonical record. What each page contains:

- Companies: funding, deployments and valuations of tracked robotics companies.
- US vs China: a metric-by-metric comparison with an editorial edge call per metric.
- R&D: robot foundation models, world models, benchmarks, research areas and the
  component stack.
- Supply chain: categories, production shares, chokepoints, companies and
  stakeholders.
- Themes (on the front page): cross-cutting trends, each marked accelerating,
  stable or slowing.
- Policy: federal, state and city records, plus proposals no government has
  adopted.

## Data (canonical — read these)

All paths are relative to https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/

Record counts below are **as of 2026-10-26** and grow as the trackers run —
treat them as a sense of scale, not a live figure. Each dataset's own
`last_updated` / `_meta.last_updated` is authoritative.

- [data/us_china.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/us_china.json): The US and China comparison. A structured document, not an array: `bluf` (headline + body), `sections[]` each holding `metrics[]`, and a `unitree_case` study. Every metric has `{id, metric, us, china, edge, sources[]}` where `edge` is one of `us` / `china` / `even` — the site's editorial edge call on that metric. 35 metrics. Start here.
- [data/supply_chain.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/supply_chain.json): Where robots and their parts are made. Structured document: `overview.bluf`, `chain_stages[]` (each with `us_position`: strong / contested / weak), `categories[]` with US/China/RoW share percentages and `chokepoints[]`, `companies[]`, `stakeholders[]`, and `production_trend[]` (annual US/China/RoW industrial-robot installations, historical observations through 2025; no country forecasts). 81 records.
- [data/companies.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/companies.json): Array of 111 robotics companies — `funding_rounds[]`, `deployments[]`, valuation, HQ, `map_category` (humanoid / brains / industrial / defense / field / service / enablers), `data_confidence` (high / medium / low), `sources[]`.
- [data/policies.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/policies.json): Array of 70 federal, state, and city policy records — bills, executive orders, regulations, incentive programs, procurement. Each has `type`, `level`, `status`, `introduced_date`, `robotics_scope` (why it matters to robotics), and `sources[]`.
- [data/news.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/news.json): Array of 1274 tracked news records; the News page sorts them newest first. Each has `date`, `source`, `source_url`, `summary`, `category` (Funding / Deployment / Policy / Competitive / Supply Chain / Geopolitics / Research), `sentiment`, `confidence`, and often an `archive_url` (Wayback snapshot).
- [data/rd.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/rd.json): The R&D tracker, captured 2026-10-26: foundation models, world models, benchmarks with their leaders, research areas, datasets, compute, and the humanoid component stack. Every entry carries `sources[]` with a capture date and a `status` (`verified` = quote read on the page; `snippet-only` = seen in a search snippet, page not read). Vendor-reported scores are flagged as such; benchmark leaders change often, so read each benchmark's `as_of`.
- [data/themes.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/themes.json): 8 cross-cutting narratives with `direction` (Accelerating / Stable / Slowing).
- [data/state_policy.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/state_policy.json): 5 state-policy themes covering what states control.
- [data/agencies.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/agencies.json): 25 federal agencies referenced by policy records.
- [data/sources.json](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/data/sources.json): Scraper configuration — which feeds are ingested.

## Pages

- [Dashboard](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/): Lead news stories, robot installations, US and China edge calls, headline KPIs, themes and the highest-valued companies.
- [US vs China](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/china.html): Metrics compared side by side, with an editorial edge call per metric.
- [Supply Chain](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/supply-chain.html): Materials, components, compute, assembly — categories, chokepoints, capacity, and the stakeholder map.
- [R&D](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/rd.html): Robot foundation models, world models, benchmarks and leaderboards, research areas, and the component stack, as in-page tabs (`?tab=` deep links).
- [Companies](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/companies.html): The market map — funding, deployments, valuations.
- [Policy](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/policies.html): In-page tabs (`?tab=` deep links): Federal (bills, regulations, incentives, procurement), States & cities (delivery-robot and AV rules, incentives, the AI preemption fight), and Potential (proposals from reports, testimony, think tanks and officials that no government has adopted, each cited).
- [Section 232: Robotics and Industrial Machinery](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/section-232-robotics.html): The October 28, 2026 proclamation explained clause by clause, the statutes it cites, its dated deadlines, the agencies and officials carrying it out, and the companies exposed.
- [SCSP AI+ Robotics Summit](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/scsp-summit.html): Event brief for Oct 14, 2026 — agenda, speaker bios, company news, recent posts, themes and policy context.
- [News](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/news.html): The tracked feed, each item cited.
- [Robotics for Energy](https://pranava0x0.github.io/roboticsleadership/energy.html): Special report — robots across power generation, the grid, nuclear cleanup, and energy R&D.

## Citing this site

Cite the page or the specific record's own `sources[]` URL. Records carry
`last_updated`; the structured datasets carry `_meta.last_updated`. Data is
curated by hand — quote the number, and link the page it came from so a reader
can check the citation. If a number matters, follow `sources[]` to see what it
actually rests on: a filing, or an outlet's reporting of one.

## Caveats, stated plainly

- Coverage is curated by one person. This is a tracker, not a census: absence of a record is not evidence of absence.
- `data_confidence` and `confidence` fields mark how well-sourced a record is. Respect them; do not present a `low` / `Medium` record as settled fact.
- Funding and valuation figures are reported values from press coverage unless a round is marked `confirmed`.
- News `category` and `sentiment` are assigned at scrape time and are occasionally wrong.
- Nothing here is investment advice.
